title: A Queue That Knows Its Maximum

concept.title: A second deque that keeps only the possible maximums
body: You want a queue with `enqueue`, `dequeue` and `max` (the largest value in the queue), all fast. Finding the maximum by scanning is O(n). Keep a **second deque** `mx` next to the queue with the values that can still become the maximum, in decreasing order.

body.code:
enqueue x:  queue.append(x)
            while mx and mx[-1] < x: mx.pop()      # smaller older values can never be the maximum
            mx.append(x)
dequeue:    v = queue.popleft()
            if mx[0] == v: mx.popleft()           # the maximum left the queue
max:        mx[0]

body: A value in the queue that is smaller than a **newer** value can never be the maximum while the newer one stays, because it leaves the queue first. So only values that are at least as large as all newer values need to be remembered. When the front value leaves and it is the front of `mx` too, remove it there as well. Equal values are kept (the test is strict: `<`), so a duplicate of the maximum is not lost.

statement: Process `n` operations on an initially empty queue. `enqueue x` adds `x` at the back. `dequeue` removes the front and prints it. `max` prints the largest value in the queue. Every line has an operation and a number; for `dequeue` and `max` the number is 0 and is ignored. The queue is not empty when `dequeue` or `max` is used. Print one line for every `dequeue` and `max`.
inputFormat: Each of the next `n` lines has an operation and a number.
outputFormat: One line for every `dequeue` and `max` operation.
constraints: There is at least one `dequeue` or `max` operation.

examples.input:
6
enqueue 3
enqueue 1
enqueue 5
max 0
dequeue 0
max 0
examples.note: The maximum is 5; the front 3 leaves; the maximum is still 5.

hints: Keep a second deque with the possible maximums, decreasing from the front to the back.
On enqueue, remove smaller values from the back of the second deque, then add the new value.
On dequeue, if the removed value equals the front of the second deque, remove it there too.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
ops = [input().split() for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: The second deque holds the values that can still be the maximum, in decreasing order. It is updated on every enqueue and dequeue, so `max` is the front of it.
solution.complexity: Amortised O(1) per operation, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
ops = [input().split() for _ in range(n)]

from collections import deque
queue = deque()
mx = deque()
out = []
for op, val in ops:
    if op == "enqueue":
        x = int(val)
        queue.append(x)
        while mx and mx[-1] < x:
            mx.pop()
        mx.append(x)
    elif op == "dequeue":
        v = queue.popleft()
        if mx[0] == v:
            mx.popleft()
        out.append(v)
    else:
        out.append(mx[0])
print("\n".join(map(str, out)))
